error.connection: Unable to connect to the gateway.
error.unable_to_calibrate:
The calibration process has encountered an issue and could not be completed successfully. Please ensure that your heating system is functioning properly and that all required sensors are connected and working correctly.

If you continue to experience issues with calibration, consider contacting us for further assistance. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.

progress.calibration:
Calibrating and finding the overshoot protection value...

Please wait while we optimize your heating system. This process may take approximately 20 minutes.

automatic_gains.description:
This feature adjusts the control parameters of your heating system dynamically, optimizing temperature control for better comfort and energy efficiency. Enabling this option allows Ally OTGW to continuously adapt and fine-tune the heating settings based on the environmental conditions. This helps maintain a stable and comfortable environment without manual intervention.

Note: If you choose not to enable automatic gains, you will need to manually enter the PID values for precise temperature control. Please ensure that you have accurate PID values for your specific heating system to achieve optimal performance.
automatic_gains.title: Automatic Gains

calibrate_system.description:
Optimize your heating system by automatically determining the optimal PID values for your setup. When selecting Automatic Gains, please note that the system will go through a calibration process that may take approximately 20 minutes to complete.

Automatic Gains is recommended for most users as it simplifies the setup process and ensures optimal performance. However, if you're familiar with PID control and prefer to manually set the values, you can choose to skip Automatic Gains.

Please note that choosing to skip Automatic Gains requires a good understanding of PID control and may require additional manual adjustments to achieve optimal performance.

menu_options.calibrate: Calibrate and determine your overshoot protection value (approx. 20 min).
menu_options.overshoot_protection: Manually enter the overshoot protection value.

calibrate_system.title: Calibrate System

calibrated.description:
The calibration process has completed successfully.

Congratulations! Your Danfoss Ally OTGW has been calibrated to optimize the heating performance of your system. During the calibration process, Ally OTGW carefully analyzed the heating characteristics and determined the appropriate overshoot protection value to ensure precise temperature control.

Overshoot Protection Value: {minimum_setpoint} °C

This value represents the maximum amount of overshoot allowed during the heating process. Ally OTGW will actively monitor and adjust the heating to prevent excessive overshooting, maintaining a comfortable and efficient heating experience in your home.

Please note that the overshoot protection value may vary depending on the specific characteristics of your heating system and environmental factors. It has been fine-tuned to provide optimal performance based on the calibration results.
calibrated.title: Calibration Completed

overshoot_protection.description:
By providing the overshoot protection value, Ally OTGW will adjust the control parameters accordingly to maintain a stable and comfortable heating environment. This manual configuration allows you to fine-tune the system based on your specific setup.

Note: If you are unsure about the overshoot protection value or have not performed the calibration process, it is recommended to cancel the configuration and go through the calibration process to let Ally OTGW automatically determine the value for optimal performance.
overshoot_protection.title: Overshoot Protection

pid_controller.description: Configure the proportional, integral, and derivative gains manually to fine-tune your heating system. Use this option if you prefer to have full control over the PID controller parameters. Adjust the gains based on your specific heating system characteristics and preferences.
pid_controller.title: Configure the PID controller manually.

sensors.title: Outside temperature
sensors.description: Select the outside temperature, which sets the base flow temperature of the boiler. A local outdoor sensor is best: if only a weather service is selected and it becomes unavailable, the boiler stays off. The room temperatures come from the Danfoss Ally TRVs, which you assign to zones in the options after this setup.

serial.description:
To establish a connection with the OpenTherm Gateway using a socket connection, please provide the following details. In the Name field, enter a name for the gateway that will help you identify it within your system.

Specify the network address of the OpenTherm Gateway in the Device field. This could be in the format of "socket://otgw.local:25238", where "otgw.local" is the hostname or IP address of the gateway and "25238" is the port number.

These settings are essential for establishing communication and integration with your OpenTherm Gateway through the socket connection. Ensure that the provided details are accurate to ensure proper functionality.
serial.title: OpenTherm Gateway ( SERIAL )

simulator.description:
This gateway allows you to simulate a boiler for testing and demonstration purposes. Please provide the following information to configure the simulator.

Note: The Simulator Gateway is intended for testing and demonstration purposes only and should not be used in production environments.
simulator.title: Simulated Gateway ( ADVANCED )

switch.description:
Please fill in the following details to set up the switch. Enter a name for the switch in the Name field, which will help you identify it within your system. Choose the appropriate entity to use for your switch from the provided options.

In the Temperature Setting field, specify the desired target temperature for your heating system. If you are using a hot water boiler, fill in the Boiler Temperature Setting with the appropriate value. For electric heating systems, enter the value 100.

These settings are essential for precise temperature control and ensuring optimal performance of your heating system. Providing the correct Temperature Setting allows for accurate regulation and helps achieve a comfortable and energy-efficient environment in your home.
switch.title: PID Thermostat with PWM ( ON/OFF )

user.description: Ally OTGW is a smart thermostat capable of auto-tuning itself to optimize temperature control. Select the mode that matches your heating system.
user.title: Danfoss Ally OTGW

manufacturer.description: We have attempted to identify the most suitable manufacturer for your heating system based on your gateway type and device information. However, if this does not match your setup, you can select a different manufacturer from the list.

data_description.dynamic_minimum_setpoint: Activates the dynamic setpoint adjustment based on the boiler's return temperature, which also helps identify if any valves are closed.
data_description.maximum_consumption: The maximum gas consumption when the boiler is active.
data_description.maximum_relative_modulation: Representing the highest modulation level for an efficient heating system.
data_description.minimum_consumption: The minimum gas consumption when the boiler is active.
data_description.sample_time: The minimum time interval between updates to the PID controller.

data.duty_cycle: Maximum Duty Cycle for Pulse Width Modulation

data_description.automatic_gains_value: The value used for automatic gains in the PID controller.
data_description.derivative: The derivative term (kD) in the PID controller, responsible for mitigating overshooting.
data_description.derivative_time_weight: A parameter to adjust the influence of the derivative term over time, particularly useful for reducing undershoot during the warm-up phase when the heating curve coefficient is correctly set.
data_description.duty_cycle: The length of one Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) on/off cycle, used only when Automatic duty cycle is off. This does not turn PWM on or off.
data_description.heating_curve_coefficient: The coefficient used to adjust the heating curve.
data_description.overshoot_hold: The minimum error a room keeps contributing while its thermostat still reports heating, so heat is requested until the thermostat itself is satisfied.
data_description.integral: The integral term (kI) in the PID controller, responsible for reducing steady-state error.
data_description.maximum_setpoint: The optimal temperature for efficient boiler operation.
data_description.proportional: The proportional term (kP) in the PID controller, responsible for the immediate response to errors.

data_description.cycles_per_hour: The maximum number of burner cycles per hour while Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) is running. This does not turn PWM on or off.
data_description.automatic_duty_cycle: How Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) times its on/off cycles. On: Ally OTGW picks the timing itself, limited by Duty Cycles per hour. Off: one fixed cycle of Maximum Duty Cycle (General) is split into on and off time. This does not turn PWM on or off: PWM runs whenever the requested flow temperature is below the Overshoot Protection Value.
data_description.sensor_max_value_age: The maximum age of the temperature sensor value before considering it as a stall.

zones.title: Zones
zones.description:
{overview}

Choose a zone to change its settings, or add and remove zones. Your changes are saved with *Save and close*.

data.zone: What do you want to do?

zone.title: Zone: {zone}

data_description.mode: How the TRVs in this zone call for heat.
data_description.minimum_open: Together only: the zone calls for heat once this many of its TRVs ask for heat.
data_description.minimum_demand: Together only: or once the valve openings (pi_heating_demand) of the TRVs asking for heat add up to this. 0 disables this rule.
data_description.maximum_wait: Together only: a TRV asking for heat on its own gets heat after this time anyway.

zone_areas.title: Add or remove zones
zone_areas.description: Select the Home Assistant areas whose Danfoss Ally TRVs this integration controls. Every area becomes a zone: its TRVs are found automatically, also when you add, move or remove TRVs later. Only areas that contain a Danfoss Ally are listed.

reset_integral.name: Reset Integral
reset_integral.description: This service resets the integrating part of the PID controller for the specified climate entity. This may be useful if the integral value has become too large or if the PID controller's performance has degraded.

pulse_width_modulation.name: Pulse Width Modulation
pulse_width_modulation.description: Force enable or disable the Pulse Width Modulation, do note that it may be turned on or off automatically right after again.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: The state you want to force.
